extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Reexamination Legal Advisors (RLA)/OPLA staff, and patent practitioners handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling inter partes reexamination proceedings at the USPTO, including the effect of federal court decisions, statutory estoppel, suspension/termination criteria, NIRC preparation, examiner amendments, reasons for patentability, and administrative checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt notification of Federal Court decisions (37 CFR 1.985(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.985(a), the patent owner in an inter partes reexamination proceeding must promptly notify the Office of any Federal Court decision involving the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must be alerted to any Federal Court decision affecting the patent. If the examiner discovers litigation or a Federal Court decision at any time during the reexamination, the fact must be brought to the attention of a Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA) of OPLA prior to any further action. The RLA will provide guidance on compliance with Office policy when there is concurrent litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final court decisions have no binding effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-final Court decision concerning a patent under reexamination shall have no binding effect on a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination of claims continues while a court decision is non-final (i.e., where appeals remain). Action in the reexamination proceeding is not suspended merely because litigation is stayed as to the patent under 35 U.S.C. 318; reexamination may still be needed to resolve patentability issues set forth in 35 U.S.C. 318.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final court holding of invalidity/unenforceability is binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the issuance of a final holding of invalidity or unenforceability by a Federal Court, the holding is binding on the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims held invalid/unenforceable will be withdrawn from consideration in the reexamination; reexamination continues as to remaining claims. If all claims are finally held invalid/unenforceable, the CRU Director will vacate the reexamination (no substantial new question of patentability) and terminate prosecution. Where claims held invalid are referenced in an Office action, use form paragraph 26.80 at the beginning of the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 26.80 — Claims held invalid by court
rubrics_metrics.description: Template for stating that particular patent claims are not being reexamined due to a final court decision holding them invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 26.80 Claims Held Invalid by Court, No Longer Being Reexamined: "Claims [1] of the [2] patent are not being reexamined in view of the final decision of [3]. Claims [1] were held invalid by the [4]." Examiner notes indicate how to fill brackets (claims, patentee, decision citation, court name). Use this paragraph when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of final court holding of validity when requester was a party
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final court decision upholding validity occurs during inter partes reexamination and the person who filed the request was a party to the litigation, the Office will discontinue examination of all claims affected by the holding of validity (for issues raised or that could have been raised by that patent owner/requester).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 37 CFR 1.907(b) applies such that all claims cannot be maintained, the order to reexamine is vacated by the CRU Director and reexamination is terminated. If 1.907(b) applies to only some claims, those claims will not be treated and the examiner’s action must point out which claims are not treated and why. Note that 1.907(b) cannot be waived since it tracks statute (35 U.S.C. 317). Consult OPLA as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of final court holding of validity when requester was not a party
rubrics_metrics.description: A final Court decision upholding validity during inter partes reexamination where the requester was not a party to the litigation will have no binding effect on the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethicon v. Quigg establishes the Office is not bound by a court’s holding of patent validity because courts and the Office use different standards of proof (clear and convincing in court vs preponderance in the Office). Deference may ordinarily be given to the court’s factual findings where the evidence before the Office and the court is the same, but claims held valid by the court may still be rejected in reexamination if sufficient reasons are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory estoppel under 35 U.S.C. 317(b) (bar on requester/privies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a final decision has been entered against a party in a civil action (arising in whole or in part under 28 U.S.C. 1338) that the party has not sustained its burden of proving invalidity, then that party and its privies may not thereafter request inter partes reexamination of any such patent claim on the basis of issues which that party or its privies raised or could have raised in such civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 317(b) is a statutory estoppel that can attach to an inter partes requester who was also a party to litigation concerning the patent. The subsection does not prevent assertion of invalidity based on newly discovered prior art unavailable to the requester and the PTO at the time of the reexamination request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority and special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 314(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: All inter partes reexamination proceedings shall be conducted with special dispatch unless otherwise provided by the Director for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director has statutory authority and discretion to suspend inter partes reexamination proceedings for "good cause." A District Court decision pending appeal on the validity of the same claims may provide good cause for suspension because of the potential for 35 U.S.C. 317(b) estoppel to attach. Decisions about suspension are fact-specific and should involve consultation with OPLA where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor A — Estoppel applies only to litigated claims
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 317(b) estoppel applies only to patent claims that were litigated in the suit (i.e., litigated claims). It does not apply to non-litigated patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-litigated claims were included in the inter partes request, the reexamination proceeds with respect to those non-litigated claims. If the patent owner later disclaims all non-litigated claims leaving only litigated claims, the proceeding should be referred to OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor B — Estoppel limited to issues raised or that could have been raised
rubrics_metrics.description: The 317(b) estoppel applies only to issues which the requester or its privies raised or could have raised in the civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel does not attach where new art/issues are raised in the reexamination request that were not and could not have been raised in the litigation. The patent owner bears the burden of showing that the art and issues applied in the request were available to the third-party requester and could have been placed in the litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor C — Estoppel attaches only after a final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The 317(b) estoppel applies only where a final decision adverse to the requester has been issued (i.e., after all appeals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is time for appeal or reconsideration, the decision is not final and estoppel does not attach. A stay/suspension of reexamination may be appropriate if litigation has advanced sufficiently and there is a sufficient probability of an adverse final decision; such matters should be discussed with OPLA on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor D — Concurrent ex parte reexamination considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a concurrent ex parte reexamination with overlapping issues, the issuance of a final Federal Court decision upholding validity during an ex parte reexamination also will have no binding effect on the ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on facts, the Office may in some instances proceed with "special dispatch" in a merged proceeding containing both inter partes and ex parte reexamination to avoid rework and increase efficiency. Such decisions should involve OPLA and depend on individual circumstances (see Ethicon guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor E — Case examples and fact-specific treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific past reexamination cases illustrate how suspensions/terminations were handled based on requester behavior and litigation posture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reexamination controls ‘093 and ‘094 were suspended due to requester delaying filing until after district court judgment and prospect of Federal Circuit appeal; other controls (‘020, ‘071, ‘072) were not suspended where facts dictated otherwise. These show that delay by requester in filing can be a reason for finding "good cause" to suspend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner litigation search and RLA consultation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is responsible for conducting a reasonable investigation to determine whether the patent has been involved in litigation (review reexamination file, patent file, STIC litigation computer search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner discovers litigation or a Federal Court decision at any time during the reexamination, the fact must be brought to the attention of an RLA of OPLA prior to any further action. The RLA will guide compliance with Office policy when there is concurrent litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances when a NIRC is appropriate (five situations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only instances when issuance of a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) is proper: (A) no timely response by patent owner to an Office action requiring response; (B) after a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) where no party timely files a notice of appeal; (C) after filing of a notice of appeal where all appellants fail to timely file an appellant brief (or complete it); (D) after a final decision by the Board where no further timely appeal or rehearing is filed; (E) after the Federal Court appeal process has been completed and case returned to examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must use Form PTOL-2068 to complete NIRC and attach examiner’s amendment as appropriate. Follow the specific procedural steps for each instance to prepare the NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of NIRC when no claims are allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where all claims are rejected or objected to in the prior Office action, the examiner will issue an NIRC indicating all claims have been canceled and terminating prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a formal examiner’s amendment canceling all live claims to PTOL-2068. In the remarks of the examiner’s amendment, point out why claims have been canceled. Since all claims are canceled, no reasons for patentability are attached. No panel review conference is needed; issuance is ministerial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of NIRC when at least one allowed claim remains
rubrics_metrics.description: If at least one claim is free of rejection/objection, the NIRC should identify patentable claims and canceled claims; rejected/objected claims are canceled by formal examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reasons for patentability for every patentable claim. Examiner prepares draft preliminary NIRC and informs CRU SPE/TC QAS of intent to issue. CRU SPE/TC QAS convenes a panel review conference; if conference confirms examiner’s decision, the NIRC is issued and signed by examiner with two conferees initialing. If not confirmed, the examiner reevaluates and issues an appropriate Office action. Panel review is not required for claims that were reviewed by the Board or a federal court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on interviews and examiner’s amendments in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews (personal and telephone) are not permitted in inter partes reexamination; examiner cannot telephone patent owner to obtain authorization to make an amendment. Examiner’s amendments may be made only where patent owner authorization is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted examiner’s amendments accompanying an NIRC include: (A) formal matters (grammar, spelling, incorrect numbers), (B) title changes, (C) cancellation of all rejected/objected claims when patent owner fails to timely respond/appeal/maintain appeal, and (D) statements withdrawing amendments if patent expired. Any change going to the merits cannot be made by examiner’s amendment with the NIRC and requires CRU Director approval, reopening prosecution, Office action suggesting change, formal amendment by patent owner, and opportunity for third-party comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment compliance requirements (37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment must comply with requirements of 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) when amending the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a portion of the text is amended more than once, the amendment should indicate all changes (insertions and deletions) relative to the current text in the patent under reexamination. Presentation of the full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed is required with 37 CFR 1.530(f) markings. The only exception is deletion of an entire claim or paragraph, which may be by statement without presenting the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability must be provided for each claim identified as patentable in the NIRC unless all claims are canceled in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the attachment to the NIRC, indicate why the claims found patentable are clearly patentable over the cited patents/printed publications. This is similar to reasons for allowance in an application (see MPEP §1302.14). Where the record is clear, examiner may refer to particular portions of the record. Use Form PTOL-476 or form paragraph 26.70 (¶ 26.70 Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation) as preferred formats. Patent owner must be notified it may submit comments on the reasons for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable vs confirmed claim terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims found patentable in reexamination are generally designated as 'confirmed'; new or amended claims are generally 'patentable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of setting forth reasons for patentability/confirmation, the examiner may use 'patentable' to refer to any claim that defines over the cited patents/printed publications. There is no need to separate 'confirmed' and 'patentable' categories when preparing reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of case for publication and required checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the inter partes reexamination file for publication in the same manner as ex parte reexamination (see MPEP §2287). Examiner must complete Examiner Checklist Reexamination form PTOL-1516; the Legal Instrument Examiner must complete Reexamination Clerk Checklist PTOL-1517.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case is reviewed by CRU SPE/TC QAS; if all in order, forwarded to RLA. After RLA review, NIRC is mailed, PALM work and scanning carried out, and the case forwarded to Office of Data Management for printing. If RLA returns case for correction, corrections must be handled timely as set by the RLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination procedural reminders (checklist A–M)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of items requiring special attention before forwarding the case for CRU SPE/TC QAS review: (A) examine all claims with a substantial new question (SNQ) of patentability; (B) no renumbering of patent claims permitted (new claims may require renumbering); (C) amendments must conform to 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(k); (D) prior art must be listed on proper forms (PTO-892, PTO-1449, PTO/SB/08A/08B/42); (E) examiner and clerk checklists must be fully completed and in agreement; (F) multiple copending reexaminations often merged; (G) copending reissue application forwarding to OPLA for potential merger; (H) reasons for patentability/confirmation are required for each patentable claim; (I) no issue fee in reexamination; (J) claims may not be amended or new claims added after patent expiration; (K) original drawings cannot be physically changed (use new sheets); (L) amended/new claims may not enlarge scope; (M) if patent expired, all amendments/added claims must be withdrawn and rejected/ objected claims canceled by examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item cites relevant MPEP sections (e.g., §2643, §2666.01, §2250, §2657, §2666.02, §2658) and emphasizes administrative compliance (forms, checklists, merging procedures, drafting of examiner’s amendments) before forwarding the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple dependent claims for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of multiple dependent claims when preparing reexamination proceeding for publication is addressed in MPEP §2287.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §2287 for detailed instructions on how to present multiple dependent claims in the reexamination certificate and related publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when all claims are canceled in the reexamination proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: When all claims in the reexamination proceeding are to be canceled (e.g., patent owner fails to timely respond or Board affirms examiner and appeal times expire), the examiner will issue an NIRC indicating all claims canceled and terminating prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach an examiner’s amendment cancelling all live claims and state the reason for cancellation in the amendment (example wording provided: cite last Office action date and statute/regulation such as 37 CFR 1.957(b) and MPEP §2666.10). Use the NIRC (Form PTOL-2068) and follow ministerial steps for termination.
